input: n is a positive integer with 2 * n within the shared collection-size bound. redEdges and blueEdges contain directed two-integer edges with endpoints in [0, n - 1]. Self-loops, parallel edges and an edge in both colors are allowed. Let E be the total number of edge rows. All input collections are ordinary finite dense arrays/lists, not subclasses, proxies, sparse arrays or accessor-backed collections; node fields, where present, are plain data fields. Strings are ordinary/primitive strings. There is no concurrent mutation or monkey-patching of standard built-ins. Every individual collection length, computed storage count and index fits [0, 4294967295], except explicit -1 sentinels. Preconditions are not checked at runtime. Actual allocation/resource capacity and completion remain qualification obligations, not guarantees from these declared bounds. JavaScript integers are primitive safe-integer Number values, excluding negative zero, NaN, infinities, fractions and BigInt.
return: Fresh length-n array of minimum edge counts for paths from node 0 whose successive edge colors alternate, using either color first. Entry 0 is zero; unreachable nodes have -1.
mutation_aliasing: Input edge arrays and all rows are unchanged. The returned scalar-distance array is newly allocated and does not alias any input. Adjacency, state distances and queue records are private. The Solution object retains no state.
numeric: A BFS state consists of node and the color of its last edge. Starting node has distance zero in both colors, permitting either first edge. Each of at most 2 * n states is reached once; discovered distances are at most 2 * n - 1 and exact. All integer inputs and computed mathematical counts (apart from opaque Python identity keys) remain within [-9007199254740991, 9007199254740991]. No bitwise coercion is used.
complexity: O(n + E + 1) time and O(n + E + 1) auxiliary/output space. Each state is expanded once; each directed edge is inspected only from the opposite-color state at its source. Head-cursor queue retains all visited state records and its full O(n) storage is counted. Bounds use bounded-word arithmetic, constant-time array indexing and amortized append/pop; output and built-in allocation costs are included.
